'''Ada Esther Yonath''' ({{langx|he|עדה יונת}}, {{IPA|he|ˈada joˈnat|pron}}; {{nee|'''Lifshitz'''}}; 22 June 1939 – 31 August 2026) was an Israeli [[crystallography|crystallographer]] and [[Nobel laureate]] in chemistry, best known for her pioneering work on the structure of [[ribosome]]s. She was the director of the Helen and Milton A. Kimmelman Center for Biomolecular Structure and Assembly of the [[Weizmann Institute of Science]].

In 2009, Yonath received the [[Nobel Prize in Chemistry]] along with [[Venkatraman Ramakrishnan]] and [[Thomas A. Steitz]] for her studies on the structure and function of the ribosome, becoming the first Israeli woman to win the [[Nobel Prize]].<ref name="JPost1019">{{cite news|url=https://www.jpost.com/Home/Article.aspx?id=156872|title=Nobel Prize Winner 'Happy, Shocked'|last=Lappin|first=Yaakov|date=7 October 2009|work=Jerusalem Post|access-date=7 October 2009|archive-date=19 February 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110219160331/http://www.jpost.com/home/article.aspx?id=156872|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Early life==
Ada Esther Lifshitz was born in the [[Geula]] quarter of [[Jerusalem]] on 22 June 1939.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.syaga.co.il/essays/borer.pdf|title=מנכ"ל המדינה (p. 4; 18.11.09 "ידיעות אחרונות") PDF|website=syaga.co.il|access-date=5 October 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120425050143/http://www.syaga.co.il/essays/borer.pdf|archive-date=25 April 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name=NYTobit/><ref name=JP0308>{{cite news|url=https://fr.jpost.com/servlet/Satellite?cid=1204546432149&pagename=JPost/JPArticle/ShowFull |title=Ada Yonath— L'Oréal-UNESCO Award |date=8 March 2008 |work=Jerusalem Post|url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120117223623/http://fr.jpost.com/servlet/Satellite?cid=1204546432149&pagename=JPost%2FJPArticle%2FShowFull |archive-date=17 January 2012 }}</ref><ref name="cv">{{Cite web | title = Israel Prize Official Site (in Hebrew) – Recipient's C.V. | url = http://cms.education.gov.il/EducationCMS/Units/PrasIsrael/Tashsab/AdaYonat/KorotHaimPropesorAdaYonat.htm | access-date = 16 September 2009 | archive-date = 18 April 2011 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20110418124241/http://cms.education.gov.il/EducationCMS/Units/PrasIsrael/Tashsab/AdaYonat/KorotHaimPropesorAdaYonat.htm | url-status = live }}</ref> Her parents, Hillel and Esther Lifshitz, were [[Zionist]] Jews who had immigrated to the [[Mandatory Palestine|British Mandate of Palestine]] (now [[Israel]]) from [[Zduńska Wola]], Poland, in 1933 before the establishment of Israel.<ref name="Hargittai2006">{{cite book | last1=Hargittai | first1=I. | last2=Hargittai | first2=M. | title=Candid Science VI: More Conversations with Famous Scientists | publisher=Imperial College Press | year=2006 | isbn=978-1-86094-885-5 | url=https://books.google.com/books?id=uYAkWldKpx8C&pg=PA390 | access-date=9 March 2021 | page=390}} (In this source the surname is spelled ''Li'''v'''shitz'')</ref> Her father was a [[rabbi]] and came from a rabbinical family.<ref name=NYTobit/> They settled in Jerusalem and ran a grocery store, but found it difficult to make ends meet while also sharing a small apartment space to live in.<ref name=NYTobit/><ref name="energy">{{cite web|url=https://www.energy.gov/articles/ada-yonath-another-pioneering-woman-science|title=Ada Yonath: Another Pioneering Woman in Science|publisher=U.S. Department of Energy|accessdate=1 September 2026|date=25 March 2011}}</ref> 

Despite her family's poverty, her parents sent her to school in the upscale [[Beit HaKerem, Jerusalem|Beit HaKerem]] neighborhood to assure her a good education. When her father died at the age of 42, the family moved to [[Tel Aviv]].<ref name="MFA0708">{{cite news|url= http://www.mfa.gov.il/MFA/Israel+beyond+politics/Israeli+professor+receives+Life+Work+Prize+for+women+in+science+28-Jul-2008.htm|title= Israeli professor receives Life's Work Prize for women in science|date= 28 July 2008|publisher= Ministry of Foreign Affairs|access-date= 31 July 2008|archive-date= 29 March 2019|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20190329195114/http://www.mfa.gov.il/MFA/Israel+beyond+politics/Israeli+professor+receives+Life+Work+Prize+for+women+in+science+28-Jul-2008.htm|url-status= dead}}</ref> Yonath assisted her mother in bringing income by babysitting or tutoring children after her father's death.<ref name=energy/>

===Education===
Yonath was accepted to [[Tichon Hadash]] high school. Since her mother could not pay the tuition, she traded her time teaching math lessons to students, which helped pay for her schooling.<ref name="jpost.com">{{cite web | last=Siegel-Itzkovich | first=Judy | title=Former 'village fool' takes the prize – Science and Environment – Jerusalem Post | website=fr.jpost.com | date=17 January 2012 | url=https://fr.jpost.com/servlet/Satellite?cid=1204546432149&pagename=JPost%2FJPArticle%2FShowFull | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120117223623/http://fr.jpost.com/servlet/Satellite?cid=1204546432149&pagename=JPost%2FJPArticle%2FShowFull | archive-date=17 January 2012 | url-status=dead | access-date=9 March 2021}}</ref><ref name="kandell" /> At a young age, she said, she was inspired by the scientist [[Marie Curie]].<ref name="currie">{{cite journal|url=https://www.shantifoundation.global/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/Vigyan-2047-vol3_iss8_Aug2026_pp19-21_Women-In-Nobel-Ada-Yonath.pdf|title=Ada Yonath: Decoded the Secret of Life|publisher=Shanti Foundation|accessdate=1 September 2026|date=August 2026|journal=Vigyan 2047|issue=8|volume=3|page=20}}</ref> However, she stressed that Curie, whom she as a child was fascinated by after reading her biography, was not her "role model".<ref name=currie/> She returned to Jerusalem for college, graduating from the [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]] with a bachelor's degree in [[chemistry]] in 1962, and a master's degree in [[biochemistry]] in 1964. In 1968, she obtained her PhD from the [[Weizmann Institute of Science]] for [[X-ray crystallography|X-ray crystallographic]] studies on the structure of [[collagen]], with Wolfie Traub as her PhD advisor.<ref>{{cite journal |date=August 2000 |title=(IUCr) European Crystallography Prize |journal=Journal of Applied Crystallography |volume=33 |issue=4 |pages=1195 |doi=10.1107/S0021889800008281 |doi-access=free}}</ref><ref name=kandell>{{Cite news |last=Kandell |first=Jonathan |date=1 September 2026 |title=Ada Yonath, Chemist and First Israeli Woman to Receive a Nobel, Dies at 87 |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/09/01/science/ada-yonath-dead.html |access-date=1 September 2026 |work=The New York Times}}</ref>

== Scientific career ==
Yonath accepted postdoctoral positions at [[Carnegie Mellon University]] (1969) and [[MIT]] (1970).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://the-tartan.org/2025/11/10/the-history-of-cmus-nobel-prize-winners/|title=The history of CMU's Nobel prize winners|work=The Tartan |location=Carnegie Mellon University, Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, United States |date=10 November 2025|accessdate=31 August 2026|archive-date=14 November 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251114114354/https://the-tartan.org/2025/11/10/the-history-of-cmus-nobel-prize-winners/|url-status=live}}</ref> While a postdoctoral researcher at MIT she spent some time in the laboratory of subsequent 1976 [[Nobel Prize in Chemistry|chemistry Nobel Prize]] winner [[William Lipscomb|William N. Lipscomb, Jr.]] of [[Harvard University]] where she was inspired to pursue very large structures.<ref name=CEN_Nov_2009/>

[[File:Ada Yonath Weizmann Institute of Science.jpg|thumb|right|Yonath at the [[Weizmann Institute of Science]]]]

In 1970, she established what was for nearly a decade the only [[protein]] crystallography laboratory in Israel. Then, from 1979 to 1984 she was a group leader with [[Heinz-Günter Wittmann]] at the [[Max Planck Institute for Molecular Genetics]] in Berlin. She was a visiting professor at the [[University of Chicago]] in 1977–78.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://news.uchicago.edu/news.php?asset_id=1729|title=New chemistry Nobelist was UChicago visiting prof, conducted research at Argonne|author=|work=The University of Chicago|access-date=27 November 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100610040216/http://news.uchicago.edu/news.php?asset_id=1729|archive-date=10 June 2010|url-status=dead|date=8 October 2009}}</ref> She headed a [[Max-Planck Institute]] Research Unit at [[DESY]] in [[Hamburg]], Germany (1986–2004) in parallel to her research activities at the Weizmann Institute.<ref>{{Cite web |title=EMBL supports the 'impossible': Mapping the ribosome |url=https://embl.org/services-facilities/technopolis/ribosome/ |access-date=31 August 2026 |website=European Molecular Biology Laboratory |language=en |archive-date=8 June 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260608180130/https://www.embl.org/services-facilities/technopolis/ribosome/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

She focused on the mechanisms underlying [[protein biosynthesis]], by ribosomal crystallography, a research line she pioneered over 20 years ago despite considerable skepticism of the international scientific community.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://nobelprize.org/nobel_prizes/chemistry/laureates/2009/speedread.html|title=The Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2009 – Speed Read|work=nobelprize.org|access-date=1 November 2009|archive-date=1 December 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171201043046/https://www.nobelprize.org/nobel_prizes/chemistry/laureates/2009/speedread.html|url-status=live}}</ref> Ribosomes translate [[RNA]] into protein and because they have slightly different structures in microbes, when compared to [[eukaryote]]s, such as human cells, they are often a target for antibiotics. In 1993, she visualized the path taken by the nascent proteins, namely the ribosomal tunnel, and recently revealed the dynamics elements enabling its involvement in elongation arrest, gating, intra-cellular regulation and nascent chain trafficking into their folding space.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.liysf.org.uk/liysf/principal-stem-lectures/professor-ada-yonath|title=Professor Ada Yonath|date=24 October 2022 |publisher=London International Youth Science Forum (LIYSF)|accessdate=31 August 2026|archive-date=20 July 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260720105719/https://www.liysf.org.uk/liysf/principal-stem-lectures/professor-ada-yonath|url-status=live}}</ref>

In 2000 and 2001, she determined the complete high-resolution structures of both ribosomal subunits and discovered within the otherwise asymmetric ribosome, the universal symmetrical region that provides the framework and navigates the process of polypeptide polymerization. Consequently, she showed that the ribosome is a [[ribozyme]] that places its substrates in [[stereochemistry]] suitable for [[peptide bond]] formation and for substrate-mediated [[catalysis]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://hasbara.co.il/resources/israeli-nobel-prize-winners-in-science/ada-yonath-ribosome-mapping-and-modern-antibiotic-design|title=Ada Yonath: Ribosome Mapping and Modern Antibiotic Design|work=Hasbara|accessdate=31 August 2026}}</ref>

[[File:Nobel Prize 2009-Press Conference KVA-15.jpg|thumb|right|Yonath at a press conference after winning the Nobel prize in 2009]]

Additionally, Yonath elucidated the modes of action of over twenty different [[antibiotic]]s targeting the ribosome, illuminated mechanisms of [[drug resistance]] and [[drug synergy|synergism]], deciphered the structural basis for antibiotic selectivity and showed how it plays a key role in clinical usefulness and therapeutic effectiveness, thus paving the way for structure-based [[drug design]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Yonath |first=Ada |date=July 2005 |title=Antibiotics Targeting ribosomes: Resistance, Selectivity, Synergism, and Cellular Regulation |journal=Annual Review of Biochemistry |volume=74 |pages=649–679 |doi=10.1146/annurev.biochem.74.082803.133130|doi-access=free |pmid=16180279 }}</ref>

For enabling ribosomal crystallography Yonath introduced a novel technique, [[cryo bio-crystallography]], which became routine in structural biology and allowed intricate projects otherwise considered formidable.<ref name="Hope">{{cite journal | last1=Hope | first1=H. | last2=Frolow | first2=F. | last3=von Böhlen | first3=K. | last4=Makowski | first4=I. | last5=Kratky | first5=C. | last6=Halfon | first6=Y. | last7=Danz | first7=H. | last8=Webster | first8=P. | last9=Bartels | first9=K. S. | last10=Wittmann | first10=H. G. | last11=Yonath | first11=A. | title=Cryocrystallography of ribosomal particles | journal=Acta Crystallographica Section B: Structural Science | publisher=International Union of Crystallography (IUCr) | volume=45 | issue=2 | date=1 April 1989 | issn=0108-7681 | doi=10.1107/s0108768188013710 | pages=190–199| pmid=2619959 | bibcode=1989AcCrB..45..190H }}</ref>

In 2009, Yonath received the [[Nobel Prize in Chemistry]] along with [[Venkatraman Ramakrishnan]] and [[Thomas A. Steitz]] for her studies on the structure and function of the ribosome, becoming the first Israeli woman to win the [[Nobel Prize]] out of ten Israeli Nobel laureates.<ref name="JPost1019"/> She also became the first woman from the Middle East to win a Nobel prize in the sciences,<ref name="Klenke">{{cite book |last=Klenke |first=Karin |title=Women in Leadership: Contextual Dynamics and Boundaries |publisher=Emerald Group Publishing Limited |year=2011 |isbn=978-0-85724-561-8 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=eJ16kb4sgS8C&pg=PA191 |page=191}}</ref> and the first woman in 45 years to win the Nobel Prize for Chemistry.<ref name="nobelprize.org 2015">{{Cite interview| last=Yonath | first=Ada E. | title=Transcript of the telephone interview with Ada E. Yonath immediately following the announcement of the 2009 Nobel Prize in Chemistry | website=nobelprize.org |date=7 October 2009 | interviewer-last=Smith | interviewer-first=Adam | url=http://www.nobelprize.org/nobel_prizes/chemistry/laureates/2009/yonath-telephone.html | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151006143911/http://www.nobelprize.org/nobel_prizes/chemistry/laureates/2009/yonath-telephone.html | archive-date=6 October 2015 | url-status=dead | access-date=9 March 2021}}</ref>

At the Weizmann Institute, Yonath was the director of the Martin S. and Helen Kimmel Professorial Chair.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wittung-Stafshede |first=Pernilla |author-link=Pernilla Wittung-Stafshede |title=Ada Yonath |url=https://www.biophysics.org/blog/ada-yonath |access-date=31 August 2026 |website=Biophysical Society |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Personal life and death==
Yonath was married to Moshe Yonath. Their marriage ended in divorce.<ref name=NYTobit/> They had one daughter, Hagit Yonath, a doctor at [[Sheba Medical Center]], and a granddaughter, Noa.<ref name="Ilani 2009">{{cite web | last=Ilani | first=Ofri | title=Israel's Prof. Ada Yonath wins Nobel Prize for Chemistry – Haaretz – Israel News | website=haaretz.com | date=3 December 2009 | url=http://www.haaretz.com:80/hasen/spages/1119626.html | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091203104630/http://www.haaretz.com/hasen/spages/1119626.html | archive-date=3 December 2009 | url-status=dead | access-date=9 March 2021 }}</ref> Yonath was the cousin of anti-occupation activist [[Ruchama Marton]] as their mothers were sisters.<ref name=JP0308/> Ada Yonath died on August 31, 2026 at the age of 87.<ref>{{Cite news |date=31 August 2026 |title=כלת פרס נובל, פרופ' עדה יונת, הלכה לעולמה |url=https://www.ynet.co.il/environment-science/article/hyx11emm00fl |access-date=31 August 2026 |work=Ynet |language=he |archive-date=31 August 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260831171137/https://www.ynet.co.il/environment-science/article/hyx11emm00fl |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="jpost">{{cite web|url=https://www.jpost.com/israel-news/article-907162|title=Nobel Prize, Israel Prize laureate, Ada Yonath, dies aged 87|work=The Jerusalem Post|accessdate=31 August 2026|date=31 August 2026|archive-date=31 August 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260831161327/https://www.jpost.com/israel-news/article-907162|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Legacy==
[[File:The Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi felicitates the Nobel laureates at the 104th Session of the Indian Science Congress, at Tirupati, Andhra Pradesh (2) (cropped).jpg|thumb|right|Yonath with [[Prime Minister of India|Indian Prime Minister]] [[Narendra Modi]] and [[Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh|Chief Minister]] [[N. Chandrababu Naidu]] at a session for the [[Indian Science Congress Association|ISCA]] in 2017]]

As the first woman since 1964 to win the Nobel Prize in chemistry, and the first since Dorothy Crowfoot Hodgkin, 45 years previously. She was also the fourth of eight women ever to win the Nobel Prize in chemistry.<ref name=":1">{{Cite Q|Q141447704}}</ref> Although Yonath once remarked, “I am a scientist, not male or female. A scientist,”<ref name=":1" /> her 2009 award was noted as a highlight for female scientists.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://forward.com/life/116219/israeli-scientist-and-grandmother-wins-nobel-prize/|title=Israeli Scientist (and Grandmother) Wins Nobel Prize in Chemistry|work=Forward|date=7 October 2009|accessdate=1 September 2026}}</ref> ''[[The Australian]]'' noted that Yonath's Nobel win was "crushing the lab's [[glass ceiling]]".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theaustralian.com.au/nation/health-science/crashing-the-labs-glass-ceiling-nobel-prize-winners/news-story/94ae6537c752a2e918cc14dd5d249cad|title=Crushing the lab's glass ceiling|work=The Australian|access-date=1 September 2026|url-access=subscription|date=7 October 2009}}</ref> Regarded as an influential Israeli scientist, Yonath helped established the first protein crystallography laboratory in Israel.<ref name=jpost/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://businessmirror.com.ph/2015/03/07/nobel-laureate-yonath-gender-not-an-issue-to-excel-in-science/|title=Nobel Laureate Yonath: Gender not an issue to excel in science|work=Business Mirror|date=7 March 2015|accessdate=1 September 2026}}</ref>

In 2018, while interviewing Yonath, [[UNESCO]] noted that her scientific research has also been "key to understanding how antibiotics work".<ref>{{cite interview|last=Yonath|first=Ada E.|interviewer-last=Nolan|interviewer-first=Cathy|url=https://www.unesco.org/en/articles/ada-e-yonath-challenge-science-climbing-mount-everest-0|title=Ada E. Yonath: 'The challenge of science is like climbing Mount Everest'|publisher=UNESCO|accessdate=1 September 2026|date=24 January 2018}}</ref>

Following her death, ''[[The New York Times]]'' noted that Yonath's mapping of the ribosome led to new designs for antibiotics.<ref name=NYTobit>{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/09/01/science/ada-yonath-dead.html|title=Ada Yonath, Chemist and First Israeli Woman to Receive a Nobel, Dies at 87|work=[[The New York Times]]|date=1 September 2026|accessdate=1 September 2026}}</ref> Her work was noted as "boundary pushing" with it having "immediate and practical consequences" for medicine and in the "fight against infectious disease".<ref name=NYTobit/> [[President of Israel|President]] [[Isaac Herzog]] noted Yonath as "one of the leading researchers in the history of Israeli science".<ref name=jpost/> ''[[The Hindu]]'' also noted Yonath's academic impact, especially in India through her engagements in academic institutions in the country.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/kerala/academic-community-mourns-nobel-laureate-ada-yonath/article71415645.ece|title=Academic community mourns Nobel laureate Ada Yonath|work=[[The Hindu]]|date=1 September 2026|accessdate=1 September 2026}}</ref>

==Awards and recognition==
[[File:Announcement Nobelprize Chemistry 2009-6.ogv|thumb|Telephone interview with Ada Yonath during the announcement of the Nobel Prize]]

Yonath was a member of the [[United States National Academy of Sciences]]; the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]]; the [[Israel Academy of Sciences and Humanities]]; the [[European Academy of Sciences and Art]] and the [[European Molecular Biology Organization]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://wis-wander.weizmann.ac.il/people/prof-ada-yonath-nobel-laureate-and-model-scientific-perseverance-has-passed-away|title=Prof. Ada Yonath, Nobel Laureate and a Model of Scientific Perseverance, Has Passed Away|work=Wis Wander|accessdate=31 August 2026|date=31 August 2026|archive-date=31 August 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260831164101/https://wis-wander.weizmann.ac.il/people/prof-ada-yonath-nobel-laureate-and-model-scientific-perseverance-has-passed-away|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 18 October 2014, Yonath was named an ordinary member of the [[Pontifical Academy of Sciences]] by [[Pope Francis]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://press.vatican.va/content/salastampa/en/bollettino/pubblico/2014/10/18/0767/01629.html|title=Rinunce e nomine|work=vatican.va |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141022070515/http://press.vatican.va/content/salastampa/en/bollettino/pubblico/2014/10/18/0767/01629.html |archive-date=22 October 2014 |language=it}}</ref>

Her awards and honors included the following:

* In 2002, [[Israel Prize]]<ref name=jpost/>
* In 2005, [[Louisa Gross Horwitz Prize]] ([[Columbia University]])<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.iucr.org/news/newsletter/volume-14/number-1/louisa-gross-horwitz-prize|title=Louisa Gross Horwitz Prize to Yonath|publisher=[[International Union of Crystallography]] (IUCR)|accessdate=31 August 2026|archive-date=9 January 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260109184948/https://www.iucr.org/news/newsletter/volume-14/number-1/louisa-gross-horwitz-prize|url-status=live}}</ref>
* In 2006, [[Wolf Prize in Chemistry]] along with [[George Feher]].<ref name=jpost/>
* In 2006, [[The EMET Prize for Art, Science and Culture]] in Life Sciences, along with Professor [[Peretz Lavie]] (Medicine) and Professor Eli Keshet (Biology)<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.emetprize.org/en-sub/laureates/life-sciences/biology/prof-ada-yonath/|title=Prof. Ada Yonath|publisher=EMET Prize|accessdate=31 August 2026}}</ref>
* In 2007, [[Paul Ehrlich and Ludwig Darmstaedter Prize]] along with [[Harry Noller]]<ref name="e811">{{cite web | title=Harry Noller Wins Award for Ribosome Work | website=City on a Hill Press | date=24 May 2007 | url=https://cityonahillpress.com/2007/05/24/harry-noller-wins-award-for-ribosome-work/ | access-date=31 August 2026 | archive-date=9 July 2024 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240709113917/https://cityonahillpress.com/2007/05/24/harry-noller-wins-award-for-ribosome-work/ | url-status=live }}</ref>
* In 2008, the [[Albert Einstein World Award of Science]] for her pioneering contributions to protein biosynthesis in the field of ribosomal crystallography and her introduction of innovative techniques in [[cryo bio-crystallography]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Albert Einstein World Award of Science 2008 |url=http://www.consejoculturalmundial.org/winners-science-adayonath.php |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140304234700/http://www.consejoculturalmundial.org/winners-science-adayonath.php |archive-date=4 March 2014 }}</ref>
* In 2009, the [[Nobel Prize in Chemistry]] (co-recipient with [[Thomas Steitz]] and [[Venkatraman Ramakrishnan]]).<ref name="Chemistry2009">{{cite web|url=http://nobelprize.org/nobel_prizes/chemistry/laureates/2009/|title=Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2009|publisher=[[Nobel Foundation]]|access-date = 7 October 2009| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20091010063802/http://nobelprize.org/nobel_prizes/chemistry/laureates/2009/| archive-date= 10 October 2009 | url-status= live}}</ref> She was the first Israeli woman to be awarded a [[Nobel Prize]].<ref name="JJ1009">{{cite news|url=http://www.jewishjournal.com/chaitech/item/ada_yonath_--_first_israeli_woman_to_win_nobel_prize_20091007/|title=Ada Yonath—First Israeli Woman to win Nobel Prize|last=Wills|first=Adam|date=7 October 2009|work=Jewish Journal|access-date=7 October 2009|archive-date=22 April 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160422153441/http://www.jewishjournal.com/chaitech/item/ada_yonath_--_first_israeli_woman_to_win_nobel_prize_20091007/|url-status=dead}}</ref>
* In 2010, [[Wilhelm Exner Medal]]<ref>{{cite web | title=Medalists Archive – ALL MEDALISTS SINCE 1921 |publisher=Wilhelm Exner Medaillen Stiftung | url=https://www.wilhelmexner.org/medalists/ | language=en | access-date=9 March 2021 | archive-date=26 February 2021 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210226101416/https://www.wilhelmexner.org/medalists/ | url-status=live }}</ref>
* In 2011, [[Marie Curie Medal]] awarded by the [[Polish Chemical Society]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ptchem.pl/pl/honors/winners-of-the-medals-and-ptchem-awards|title=Laureaci Medali i Nagród PTChem|access-date=22 February 2020|archive-date=29 March 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250329194338/https://ptchem.pl/pl/honors/winners-of-the-medals-and-ptchem-awards|url-status=dead}}</ref>
* In 2013 she became a member of the [[German Academy of Sciences Leopoldina]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Ada Yonath|url=https://www.leopoldina.org/mitgliederverzeichnis/mitglieder/member/Member/show/ada-yonath/|publisher=German Academy of Sciences Leopoldina|access-date=26 May 2021|archive-date=26 May 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210526213449/https://www.leopoldina.org/mitgliederverzeichnis/mitglieder/member/Member/show/ada-yonath/|url-status=live}}</ref>
* In 2015, she was awarded Honorary Doctorates from the [[University of Southern California]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=Past Recipients – Honorary Degrees |url=https://honorarydegrees.usc.edu/past-recipients/ |access-date=7 June 2024 |website=honorarydegrees.usc.edu |archive-date=5 October 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201005015605/https://honorarydegrees.usc.edu/past-recipients/ |url-status=live }}</ref> the De La Salle University, Manila/Philippines; the Joseph Fourier University, Grenoble/France; the [[Medical University of Lodz]], Lodz/Poland; and the University of Warwick, UK.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www2.warwick.ac.uk/services/gov/hongrads/summer2015|title=Honorary Graduand Orations – Summer 2015|website=www2.warwick.ac.uk|access-date=2 September 2015|archive-date=2 January 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190102095123/https://warwick.ac.uk/services/gov/hongrads/summer2015|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title = Uniwersytet Medyczny w Łodzi|url = http://www.umed.pl/pl/index1.php?dir=akt&mn=tresc&txt=1750|website = www.umed.pl|access-date = 1 May 2015|archive-date = 4 March 2016|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20160304115917/http://www.umed.pl/pl/index1.php?dir=akt&mn=tresc&txt=1750|url-status = dead}}</ref>
*In 2018, [[Elizabeth Cabezas]], [[President of the National Assembly of Ecuador|President of the Ecuadorian National Assembly]], presented Yonath with the Presea "Asamblea Nacional de la República del Ecuador, Dra. Matilde Hidalgo de Procel" (National Assembly of Ecuador Dr. Matilde Hidalgo de Procel Medal) for scientific merit.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2 August 2018 |title=La Asamblea condecora a la israelí Ada Yonat, premio Nobel de Química |url=https://www.elcomercio.com/actualidad/politica/politica-asambleanacional-condecoracion-adayonat-premionobel/ |access-date=2 September 2026 |work=[[El Comercio (Ecuador)|El Comercio]]|language=Spanish}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.jta.org/2018/08/06/israel/ecuadors-national-congress-honors-israeli-nobel-laureate|title=Ecuador honors first Israeli woman to win the Nobel Prize|publisher=[[Jewish Telegraphic Agency]] |accessdate=1 September 2026|date=6 August 2018|last=Gilban|first=Marcus M.}}</ref>
* In 2018, she was awarded an Honorary Doctorate from [[Carnegie Mellon University]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cmu.edu/leadership/president/campus-comms/2018/2018-03-29.html|title=Commencement Speakers and Honorary Degree Recipients – Leadership – Carnegie Mellon University|website=www.cmu.edu|language=en|access-date=21 September 2018|archive-date=29 March 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190329195126/https://www.cmu.edu/leadership/president/campus-comms/2018/2018-03-29.html|url-status=live}}</ref>
* In 2020, she was elected a [[Foreign Member of the Royal Society]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org/people/Ada-Yonath-25413/|title=Ada Yonath|publisher=Royal Society|access-date=19 September 2020|archive-date=5 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200605144654/https://royalsociety.org/people/Ada-Yonath-25413/|url-status=live}}</ref>
* In 2023, she was awarded an Honorary Doctorate from the [[Jagiellonian University]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://en.uj.edu.pl/en_GB/about-university/ju-awards/honorary-doctorate |title=Honorary Doctorate |website=en.uj.edu.pl |access-date=28 May 2023 |archive-date=3 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230603041122/https://en.uj.edu.pl/en_GB/about-university/ju-awards/honorary-doctorate |url-status=live }}</ref>
* In 2024, she was awarded an Honorary Doctorate from the [[Technion – Israel Institute of Technology|Technion]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=shelleys |date=4 June 2024 |title=Honorary Doctorate Awardees |url=https://www.technion.ac.il/en/blog/honorary-doctorate-awardees/ |access-date=11 June 2025 |website=הטכניון-מכון טכנולוגי לישראל |language=en-US |archive-date=20 June 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250620145105/https://www.technion.ac.il/en/blog/honorary-doctorate-awardees/ |url-status=live }}</ref>
